name: NVIDIA DGX Spark
notes: Bandwidth, not capacity, decides speed here: 273 GB/s shared between CPU and GPU.
Dense 70B-class lands around 2.7 tok/s. A 35B MoE with 3B active reaches 60-100 tok/s. MoE wins on this box by 5-8x at equal quality.
big.LITTLE: pin containers to the X5 cores (--cpuset-cpus 5-9,15-19) or the scheduler lands on A725s about half the time. Measured +2-7% decode.
100B+ MoE needs the disk-mapped embedding-table trick to fit at all.
The box power-caps and drifts under sustained load: essay throughput fell 19.5 -> 18 tok/s over about an hour of heavy benching. Re-baseline in-session.

compute.note: NVIDIA publishes only the FP4-sparse theoretical peak (up to 1 PFLOP, using sparsity) for GB10; dense FP32/FP16/FP8 rates are not published, so they stay null. Decode on this box is bandwidth-bound: 273 GB/s sets the roofline.

storage.note: 4 TB per the datasheet; sequential read rate not published

thermal.note: 140 W is the GB10 chip TDP (CPU+GPU); 240 W is the system power supply rating

sources.note: official specifications: 128 GB LPDDR5x unified, 256-bit, 273 GB/s, 20-core Arm (10x Cortex-X925 + 10x Cortex-A725), up to 1 PFLOP FP4 (sparse), GB10 TDP 140 W, 240 W PSU, 4 TB NVMe M.2
